description.narrative: The objective of the Emergency Response to COVID-19 (Coronavirus) Program for Indonesia is to prevent, detect and respond to the threat posed by COVID-19 and strengthen national systems for public health preparedness. The Program will focus on 4 results areas. Results Area 1 will address hospital and health system readiness and systemic improvements in the quality of care. The Program will support the expanded network of Ministry of Health (MOH)-owned health facilities that have been designated as COVID-19 referral hospitals. It will ensure that they are fully equipped to manage and treat the increase in severe respiratory illness and critical care patients. Results Area 2 will strengthen the GOI's (Government of Indonesia) public health laboratory and surveillance systems. The Program will support the development and the ability to maintain external quality assurance mechanism for the entire installed COVID-19 testing capacity, backed by national guidelines for laboratories adhering to BSL2 (Biosafety Level) or higher standards, covering sample collection, transportation, and laboratory testing procedures. Results Area 3 will facilitate communication and coordination for better pandemic response and preparedness. The Program recognizes the need for the MOH to coordinate with other sectors and will support the development and establishment of mechanisms for communication of COVID-19 test results (in coordination with the subnational level), support from the MOH to BNPB (National Disaster Risk Management Agency) and other agencies in developing messages on personal hygiene promotion and other preventive communications. The Program also supports the coordination with other sectors in the development and/or the revision of the National Pandemic Preparedness Plan to increase the readiness for the next threat of any outbreak or pandemic. Results Area 4 will provide technical information to inform communications and counter misinformation. As the Program-for-Results (PforR) focuses on MOH activities, Results Area 4 is partially beyond the PforR scope to the extent that this function is now handled by BNPB, which is also the platform mentioned under Results Area 1. The MOH's support to Results Areas 1 and 4 is included in the Program boundaries limited to MOH activities, but not the remaining activities of this multisectoral platform. Expenses at the subnational level are also not included in the PforR scope.
To prevent, detect and respond to the threat posed by COVID-19 and strengthen national systems for public health preparedness in Indonesia.

MOH supports the creation of a multi-sectoral coordination mechanism for COVID-19 response
Enhanced community engagement and communication (as measured by the number of interactions with the COVID-19 phone line)
Number of beds temporarily converted for patient isolation and/or low intensity medical care
Number of simulation exercises undertaken as per updated national pandemic preparedness plan
Reduced service readiness gap in treating severe respiratory illness patients (as measured by the available number of intensive care beds equipped as per national protocol)
Cumulative number of COVID-19 suspect cases tested by PCR or rapid molecular testing, disaggregated by sex
Cumulative number of cases MOH counters COVID-19 vaccine related misinformation and posts on its website
Strengthened laboratory capacity (measured as total capacity for quality assured tests per day)
Cumulative number of website visitors to the COVID-19 communication portal set up by the Government of Indonesia
A surveillance mechanism for community-based reporting of outbreaks and new illnesses among humans and animals is functional
Concrete measures to support and compensate health professionals for added COVID-19 related workload and risk are implemented
Infection prevention and clinical management protocols developed and disseminated to all non-referral facilities
Improved reporting and surveillance system (measured as the availability of an improved surveillance system that incorporates lessons from the COVID-19 response experience)
Number of functional locations with remote temperature monitoring system
Maintaining essential non COVID-19 services (% decline of number of completed fourth ANC services delivered in the previous quarter as a proportion to the corresponding quarter in 2019)
